section_summary: This section covers United States State Department and SCAP records from November 1945 to April 1949 regarding the rehabilitation, administration, and output of Japan's coal mining industry. It documents initial production collapses caused by labor and material shortages, emergency coal allocations to South Korea, the establishment of the Japanese Coal Board, and parliamentary debates over the Coal Bill. Subsequent records detail SCAP surveillance of Hokkaido coal fields, labor disputes, price adjustments, and technical mechanization programs including American engineering surveys and study tours.

subfiles.about: Inquiry regarding potential monthly coal exports from Japan in 1946 and associated American costs.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: State Department requests estimates of Japan's 1946 coal export capacity under maximum effort and the potential cost to the United States.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram 94 to Tokyo Regarding Japanese Coal Exports
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo (Atcheson for Willoughby from Martin)

subfiles.about: Report on Japanese coal production difficulties, export prospects to Korea and Hong Kong, and supply shortages.
subfiles.from: Office of the US Political Adviser, Tokyo (Atcheson for Martin from Willoughby)
subfiles.summary: Reports that early 1946 exports are impossible due to mine labor and supply shortages, though late-year exports might reach 500,000 tons monthly.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram 144 on Coal Industry Rehabilitation and Export Prospects

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Natural Resources Section Report Number 3 on the Japanese coal mining industry.
subfiles.from: George Atcheson, Jr., US Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits Natural Resources Section Report No. 3 regarding basic problems of the Japanese coal mining industry to supplement recent telegrams.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 59: Japanese Coal Exports

subfiles.about: Comprehensive analysis of declining Japanese coal output, supply shortages, labor crises, and occupation needs.
subfiles.from: Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Details the collapse of Japanese coal output to 600,000 tons in October 1945 against requirements of 1.1 million tons. Identifies primary causes as severe labor shortages following the repatriation of Korean and Chinese miners, food rationing deficits, and acute shortages of explosives, wire rope, and nails. Outlines emergency measures taken by the Eighth Army to allocate materials and restore mine communications.
subfiles.title: Report No. 3: Basic Problems of the Coal Mining Industry in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Imperial Ordinance No. 705 establishing the Japanese Coal Board.
subfiles.from: Office of the US Political Adviser, Tokyo (WSebald)
subfiles.summary: Transmits English translation of Imperial Ordinance No. 705 placing coal, semi-coal, gas, and coke under the new Coal Board.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 205: Imperial Ordinance No. 705: Organization of the Coal Board

subfiles.about: Japanese government ordinance creating and structuring the Coal Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
subfiles.from: Emperor Hirohito, Prime Minister Kijuro Shidehara, and Commerce Minister Sankuro Ogasawara
subfiles.summary: Establishes the Coal Board's administrative structure, personnel ranks, bureaus (General Affairs, Production, Distribution), advisory council, and amendments to Commerce Ministry regulations.
subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 705: Ordinance for the Organization of the Coal Board

subfiles.about: Urgent request for an allocation of bituminous coal to prevent the economic collapse of southern Korea.
subfiles.from: USAFIK Korea (Hodge for Bruce thru Langdon)
subfiles.summary: Urges monthly allocation of 160,000 metric tons of bituminous coal for South Korean railroads and essential industries to avoid economic collapse.
subfiles.title: Seoul Telegram TFGCT 487 on South Korean Bituminous Coal Requirements
subfiles.to: CINCAFPAC Tokyo and War Department for State Department

subfiles.about: Guidance on the appropriate government agency for coal export license applications.
subfiles.from: Karl L. Anderson, Assistant Chief, International Resources Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Refers Morgan Fuel Corporation's application to export bunker coal to Ceuta to the Department of Commerce Office of International Trade.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Morgan Fuel Corporation on Coal Export Licensing
subfiles.to: Everett B. Morgan, President, Morgan Fuel Corporation

subfiles.about: Criticism of unilateral War Department messages allocating coal to Spain and Japan without regard to export ceilings.
subfiles.from: L. Lister, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Criticizes unilateral War Department telegrams proposing coal allocations to Spain and Japan without coordinating with established international export controls.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on War Department Messages Concerning Coal Allocations

subfiles.about: Transmittal and summary of discussions with Japanese officials regarding coal production, labor problems, electric power, and trade.
subfiles.from: Office of the US Political Adviser, Tokyo (Bushner and Lawrence)
subfiles.summary: Transmits and summarizes a dinner discussion with Commerce Minister Mizutani and Board of Trade President Nagai concerning coal output, controversial labor laws, power shortages, and foreign trade expansion.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1484: Transmittal of Memorandum of Conversation with Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: Detailed record of dinner discussions between US Foreign Service officers and Japanese officials on economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.from: Rolland H. Bushner and W. Henry Lawrence, Jr., Foreign Service Officers
subfiles.summary: Records extensive discussions between American diplomats and Japanese officials including Minister Mizutani and Kotaro Nagai. Topics covered include coal production bottlenecks, miners' labor discipline, criticism of occupation-sponsored labor legislation, parliamentary disorder over the Coal Bill, and severe electric power deficits. Nagai also discussed foreign trade operations, merchant shipping tonnage restrictions, and proposed an Asian Marshall Plan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation Concerning Coal Production, Labor Legislation, and Foreign Trade
subfiles.to: Office of the US Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Request for a copy of the publication 'Administration of coal production in Japan'.
subfiles.from: Arthur C. Pulling, Director, Harvard Law School Library
keywords: Administration of coal production in Japan
subfiles.summary: Thanks the Department for a complimentary publication and requests a copy of 'Administration of coal production in Japan'.
subfiles.title: Letter from Harvard Law School Library Requesting Report on Coal Production

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a requested State Department report on Japanese coal production administration.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Associate Chief, Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
keywords: Administration of Coal Production in Japan
subfiles.summary: Encloses a used copy of 'Administration of Coal Production in Japan' in response to the library's request.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State Transmitting Coal Production Report to Harvard Law School
subfiles.to: Arthur C. Pulling, Director, Harvard Law School Library

subfiles.about: Reporting on coal production problems in Hokkaido, labor union attitudes, and the necessity of price adjustments.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, US Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (WHLawrence, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Transmits a joint SCAP-Japanese investigation of Hokkaido coal mines, emphasizing management failings, union disputes, and the necessity of adjusting official coal prices so operators can make profits.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 380: Coal Production in Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Three-part report analyzing the decline in Hokkaido coal output, union wage pacts, and management-labor problems at Yayoi mine.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Presents findings of SCAP and Japanese inspection teams investigating coal mines across Hokkaido. Part I attributes production declines to lack of spirit and poor management rather than material shortages. Part II highlights the new Zen Sekitan agreement, grievance machinery schools, and revised production quotas. Part III details an inspection of Yayoi mine, criticizing management deficiencies and union slowdowns while urging increased miner productivity.
subfiles.title: Press Release: Report and Conclusions of SCAP and Japanese Coal Teams Touring Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Duplicate record copy of Despatch No. 380 concerning Hokkaido coal production and economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, US Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (WHLawrence, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Despatch No. 380 transmitting findings on Hokkaido coal production, labor problems, and price policy adjustments.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 380 (DC/R Control Copy): Coal Production in Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Assessment of prospects for meeting the 36-million-ton coal production target, mine mechanization plans, and political implications.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, US Political Adviser, Tokyo (WHLawrence, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Reports optimism that Japan's 36-million-ton coal goal can be reached, detailing field team surveillance, mine mechanization initiatives, American aid conditions, and Minister Mizutani's political perspectives.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 560: Attainment of 1948 Goal for Coal Production

subfiles.about: Announcement of favorable prospects for achieving the 36-million-ton annual coal production goal.
subfiles.from: M. A. Wyatt, Coal Coordinator, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Asserts that revised coal prices, field surveillance teams, and incentive goods will enable Japan to achieve its 36-million-ton coal target.
subfiles.title: Statement by Mr. M. A. Wyatt, Coal Coordinator, for Press Conference

subfiles.about: Editorial urging Japan to match American economic assistance with effective self-help and tangible production results.
subfiles.from: Nippon Times (reprinting Asahi editorial of August 20, 1948)
subfiles.summary: Editorial urging the Japanese people to utilize American rehabilitation funds effectively through diligent self-help rather than mere verbal gratitude.
subfiles.title: Nippon Times Editorial Reprint: 'How to Meet U.S. Assistance'

subfiles.about: Cabinet decision to accelerate coal mine mechanization to achieve production targets and save labor.
subfiles.from: Mainichi (translated by M. Yasutake)
subfiles.summary: Details the Japanese Cabinet's program to establish a mechanization headquarters, test modern mining machinery in 27 mines, and consult foreign technicians.
subfiles.title: Translation of Mainichi Article: 'Coal Mine Mechanization Speeded'

subfiles.about: Transmittal of SCAP Economic and Scientific Section documents concerning plans to raise coal output to 42 million tons.
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser, US Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (CHBoehringer)
subfiles.summary: Transmits an ESS staff study and radio message regarding EROA mining machinery funding, recruitment of American engineering experts, and proposed Japanese study tours in the United States.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 208: Staff Study on Increased Coal Production

subfiles.about: Plan to sponsor an educational survey mission of Japanese mining engineers to the United States to study modern mechanization.
subfiles.from: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Recommends sending a ninety-day mission of six Japanese mining engineers to inspect modern American coal mines and equipment manufacturers in seven states to boost domestic production toward 42 million tons.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Chief of Staff: Staff Study on Increased Coal Production

subfiles.about: Request for Department of the Army assistance in contracting a qualified American engineering firm to inspect Japanese coal mines.
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP (approved by W. F. Marquat / R. M. Levy)
subfiles.summary: Reviews survey proposals from Allen and Garcia and Antonin Raymond, and requests Army assistance to contract a qualified firm to inspect 58 Japanese mines within four months for under sixty thousand dollars.
subfiles.title: SCAP Outgoing Radio W-84574 on Engineering Survey of Japanese Coal Industry
subfiles.to: Department of the Army (for CSCAD ECON)
